'''''Pinaropappus roseus''''', the '''white rocklettuce''', is a [[species]] of [[wildflower]] native to the [[New World]]. It belongs to the [[family (taxonomy)|family]] [[Asteraceae]].<ref name="kew" />

==Discription==

''Pinaropappus roseus'', except for its white to pink flowers, is similar to and somewhat closely related to the [[dandelion]]. Here are noteworthy features helpful for seeing the distinguishing features of ''Pinaropappus roseus'':<ref name="baj">{{cite journal
| last = Calderón de Rzedowski
| first = Graciela
| title = Compositae trubu Lactuceae
| journal = Flora del Bajío y de Regiones Adyacentes
| volume =54
| pages = 35-37
| publisher = Instituto de Ecología, A.C. (INECOL)
| location = Pátzcuaro, Michoacán, México
| date = August 1997
| language = Spanish
| url = http://inecolbajio.inecol.mx/floradelbajio/documentos/fasciculos/ordinarios/Compositae%2054.pdf
| access-date = June 22, 2026}}</ref><ref name="fna">{{cite web
| url = http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=1&taxon_id=220010472
| title = Pinaropappus roseus (Lessing) Lessing. In Flora of North America North of Mexico (FNA)
| last = Bogler
| first = David J.
| volume = 21
| location = St. Louis, MO & Harvard University Herbaria, Cambridge, MA, USA
| publisher = New York and Oxford: Oxford University Press via eFloras.org
| access-date = June 22, 2026
}}</ref>

*Its 1-20+ stems  stand up to {{cvt|65.5|cm|frac=2}} high, but usually are shorter and often the plants grow in colonies. When injured, body parts exude a white [[latex]]. The woody [[taproot]] grows deep into the soil. Unlike Dandelions, the stems bear a few leaves. 

*Upper leaves are small and slender, with smooth margins but leaves arising at the base often bear some low teeth and may be shallowly lobed. Lower leaves may be up to {{cvt|12|cm|frac=2}} long and {{cvt|3|cm|frac=4}} wide. All leaves are hairless or nearly so.

*[[Asteraceae#Floral_heads|Floral heads]] consist of up to 60 flat, petal-like "ray florets" with white to pink [[Petal#Corolla|corollas]] up to {{cvt|25|mm|frac=8}} long. Green   [[Bract#Involucral_bracts|involucral bracts]] below the florets form a cuplike "involucre." The bracts, up to {{cvt|20|mm|frac=8}} long, are of unequal size and are arranged in spirals with their margins overlapping one another. Their pointed tips are dark brown.

*Very slender, one-seeded, cypsela-type [[Fruit (plant structure)|fruits]] up to {{cvt|8|mm|frac=16}} tall are pale brown. Each is topped by a [[Pappus (botany)|pappus]] consisting of up to 60 tawny or yellowish-brown [[bristles]] up to {{cvt|10|mm|frac=16}} long.

Apparently the corolla color varying from white to pink is not of taxonomic importance. It is reported that white flowers take on a pinkish hue as they age.<ref name="tx">{{cite web
| url = https://www.wildflower.org/plants/result.php?id_plant=PIROR
| title = Pinaropappus roseus var. roseus
| website = Lady Bird Johnson Wildflower Center
| location = Austin, TX, USA
| publisher = The University of Texas at Austin
| access-date = June 23, 2026 
}}</ref>

==Distribution==

In the [[Southwestern United States]], ''Pinaropappus roseus'' occurs in the states of Arizona, New Mexico, Oklahoma and Texas. In Mexico it is found nearly throughout, except in the [[Baja California Peninsula]] and the [[Yucatan Peninsula]].<ref>{{cite web
| url = https://www.worldplants.de/world-plants-complete-list/complete-plant-list/?name=Pinaropappus-roseus#plantUid-316162
| title = Search results: ''Pinaropappus roseus'' (Less.) Less.
| last         = Hassler
| first        = Michael
| date = May 20, 2026
| website =  www.worldplants.de.
| publisher = World Plants. Synonymic Checklist and Distribution of the World Flora
| access-date = June 22, 2026
}}</ref>

==Habitat==

In the USA, ''Pinaropappus roseus'' occurs in open [[limestone]] areas, along roads, on cliffs and in open grassy flats at elevations from {{cvt|50|-|2600|m}}.<ref name ="fna" /> In highland central Mexico it occurs in [[Secondary succession|secondary]] vegetation derived from various vegetation types, and sometimes in [[Ruderal species|disturbed, weedy areas]] up to {{cvt|2900|m}} in elevation.<ref name ="baj" />

==Flowering time==

''Pinaropappus roseus'' flowers open in early morning and may close by midmorning.<ref name="tx" /> In central Mexico the species can be found flowering throughout the year, but mainly from April to September.<ref name ="baj" />

==In traditional medicine==

In the [[Sierra Norte de Oaxaca]] region of Mexico's [[Oaxaca]] state, where ''Pinaropappus roseus'' is known as ''espule'', ''chipule'', or ''chipulillo'', it is used to treat vomiting and measles.<ref>{{cite journal

| journal = Neotropical Biodiversity Journal
| volume = 10
| issue = 1
| pages = 1-14
| date = 2025
| url = https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Mario-Suarez-Mota/publication/399047585_Climate_Change_Influence_on_the_Distribution_of_Four_Plant_Medicinal_Species_from_the_Sierra_Norte_of_Oaxaca_Mexico/links/695ed1cc0c98040d4828e0fe/Climate-Change-Influence-on-the-Distribution-of-Four-Plant-Medicinal-Species-from-the-Sierra-Norte-of-Oaxaca-Mexico.pdf
| access-date = June 22, 2026}}</ref> In Oaxaca and [[Puebla]] states also it is used for skin problems, especially rashes on newborn babies. For this latter use the entire plant is boiled and the water is used to bathe the baby. After bathing the baby is given a "tea" prepared from the leaves, with a little sugar added to counter the bitter taste. In [[Morelos]] state, the plant's white sap is applied to white blotches which appear on the face and hands.<ref>{{cite web

==Taxonomy==

In 1832 [[Christian Friedrich Lessing]] formally named and described ''Pinaropappus roseus'' as he erected a new genus for it, ''Pinaropappus''. In 1830 Lessing himself had described the new species ''Achyrophorus roseus'', upon which in 1832 ''Pinaropappus roseus'' was based. In establishing ''Pinaropappus'' he noted that it  was different from ''Achyrophorus'' because of its species' hairy, sordid, and not manifestly pale-colored pappus.<ref>{{cite book
| last = Lessing
| first = Chr. Fr.
| title = Synopsis generum Compositarum earumque dispositionis novae tentamen monographiis multarum capensium interjectis
| date = 1832
| pages = 143
| language = Latin
| url =https://bibdigital.rjb.csic.es/viewer/13218/?offset=#page=7&viewer=picture&o=bookmark&n=0&q= }}</ref> Later  ''Achyrophorus'' was lumped into the genus ''[[Hypochaeris]]''.<ref>{{cite web
| url = https://powo.science.kew.org/results?q=Achyrophorus
| title = ''Achyrophorus'' Adans.
| website = Plants of the World Online
| location = United Kingdom
| publisher = Royal Botanic Gardens Kew
| access-date = June 23, 2026
}}</ref>

===Infraspecies===

In 2026, these two varieties were accepted:<ref name="kew" />

*''Pinaropappus roseus'' var. ''maculatus'' [[McVaugh]] -- in the Mexican states of [[Coahuila]] and [[Nuevo León]]
*''Pinaropappus roseus'' var. ''roseus'' -- range of the species

===Etymology===
The genus name ''Pinaropappus'' derives from the Greek ''pinario'' meaning "dirty, squalid," plus ''pappos'', thus the genus name alludes to the dingy color the taxon's pappuses.<ref>{{cite web
| url = http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=1&taxon_id=242357910
| title = Pinaropappus Lessing. In Flora of North America North of Mexico (FNA)
| last = Bogler
| first = David J.
| volume = 21
| location = St. Louis, MO & Harvard University Herbaria, Cambridge, MA, USA
| publisher = New York and Oxford: Oxford University Press via eFloras.org
| access-date = June 23, 2026
}}</ref>

The species name ''roseus'' is based on the Latin ''roseus'', one definition of which is "rose-colored, red." This alludes to the pink hue of many corollas of the species.<ref>{{cite web
| url = https://latin-dictionary.net/definition/33716/roseus-rosea-roseum
| title = Latin definition for: roseus, rosea, roseum
| website = latin-dictionary.net
| publisher = Kevin D. Mahoney and the Latdict Group
| access-date = June 23, 2026
}}</ref>
